An application can pin the validated umbrella release with SwiftPM’s

Then import the library:

Use explicit settings when you need custom headers, a custom base URL, a mock transport, or per-environment credentials.
Independent modular packages
Section titled “Independent modular packages”
All 52 independent packages are published: core, 49 provider adapters, MCP and UI. Core and Anthropic are at
1.3.0

1.1.0

1.0.0

catalog

3.0 migration guide
for native imports, configuration and compatibility details.

Anthropic uses
SwiftAIAnthropic
and
AnthropicProviderSettings
. A generic compatible endpoint uses
SwiftAIOpenAICompatible
with
OpenAICompatibleProviderSettings(name:baseURL:...)
. Native factories accept
configuration:
; the 3.x compatibility API continues to accept
settings:
. Native clients pass model objects or use explicit registries; core does not initialize an implicit Gateway.
The canonical repository contains complete offline
AnthropicOnly
,
OpenAICompatibleOnly
,
OpenAIOnly
and
MixedProviders
examples. OpenAI shares chat/completion, embedding and image wire code with the compatible package; selecting it does not require unrelated providers, MCP or UI. See the
3.0 migration guide
.
Provider versions can be selected independently as long as their shared dependency requirements intersect. SwiftPM resolves one version per package identity. Swift release numbers do not track npm release numbers. Applications should commit their
Package.resolved
; reusable libraries should normally express compatible ranges.
The 3.2 umbrella shares model and request types with the modular packages and preserves the ordinary
import SwiftAISDK
API. Existing 2.x tags remain usable, but their separately defined types cannot be mixed with modular values. Moving modules is not a binary compatibility guarantee; rebuild your application. The
tested 3.2 release set
records the complete dependency selection.
The 3.2 release adds queued steering and ordered UI replay, native URL transcription and word timings, uploaded-video descriptors, request-origin privacy and provider request/stream fixes. Existing exhaustive switches must handle the new documented enum cases. See the
weekly audit
for every npm/Swift version, verified release ref and retained gap.

trueMinimumCoverage.scope: All52 current standalone source trees compile at their true version-specific minimum graph. The catalog-wide checker provides48 exact minima plus all latest/mixed/umbrella checks; four old-dependency graphs are independently supplemented, including the unchanged actual public Vercel1.0 tag with identical current owning source.
trueMinimumCoverage.versionScope: Catalog version fields are synthetic rehearsal tags for the current source trees, not a list of public releases. Unchanged ByteDance 1.0.0, Hugging Face 1.1.0, LMNT 1.0.0 and Vercel 1.0.0 were not republished. Actual public versions, immutable refs and public-consumer evidence are recorded separately in publication/exports and public consumer verification.
